title: Tenant communications — compact replay instructions and status snippets
body:
Purpose:
This working draft is a compact, customer-facing communications + self-serve replay kit for tenants affected by short-lived inference degradations. The goal is to: (1) give product/partner teams a short status page/alert copy set they can publish quickly, (2) provide an evidence/replay package customers can use to validate impact, and (3) offer recommended remediation instructions for common client behaviours (retries, streaming sessions, structured outputs).

Context / high-level summary (to place on status page or in an email):
- Incident window: 2029-04-12 03:22 — 2029-04-12 06:18 UTC (approx).
- Impact: intermittent 5xx and truncated streaming responses for a subset of requests routed through the eu-west-1 pool. Estimated affected tenant subset: ~2.8% of active tenants during the window.
- Short cause summary (customer-facing): a routing misconfiguration caused a small set of requests to be routed to a model variant that had a stale KV cache handling regression; this induced truncated streaming and 503s under specific prefix patterns.

Suggested minimal status page flow (3 short updates you can copy/paste):
1) Initial (detect):
- Title: Partial service disruption affecting streaming and some requests
- Body: We are investigating reports of intermittent failed or truncated responses for some inference requests. Impact appears limited to a small subset of requests in the EU region. Customers may see increased errors (5xx) or incomplete streamed outputs. Our engineers are actively investigating. We will post an update within 30 minutes.

2) Progress (mitigation in place):
- Title: Mitigation deployed — progressive recovery in progress
- Body: We have deployed a mitigation that routes affected requests to a compatible model variant and rolled back a routing configuration change. Error rates and truncated streams are decreasing. Some customers may still experience intermittent failures while traffic shifts. If you continue to see issues after 30 minutes, please open a support ticket and include the replay package (instructions below).

3) Resolved / follow-up:
- Title: Incident resolved — post-incident guidance
- Body: The routing issue has been resolved and normal service has been restored for affected requests. We continue to monitor. If you believe you experienced data loss or persistent truncated outputs, please provide the replay package and tenant time ranges; we will prioritize verification.

Customer-facing timeline (compact, bullet form):
- 03:22 UTC — Monitoring alert triggered (elevated 5xx and streaming truncation spike).
- 03:30 UTC — Triage team confirmed region-specific pattern; on-call engaged.
- 03:58 UTC — Rollback of recent routing config rolled out to a subset (canary).
- 04:25 UTC — Canary showed reduced errors; mitigation expanded.
- 05:10 UTC — Global rollout of mitigation complete; routing flows stabilized.
- 06:18 UTC — Monitoring shows metrics back to baseline; incident transitioned to postmortem.

Self-serve evidence / replay package (what we ask customers to collect):
Include these items when filing a support ticket so we can validate and replay the tenant’s requests quickly:
- Tenant ID (required).
- Approximate UTC time ranges where you observed errors (start/end).
- Example request ids / session ids (if available).
- Export of client-side logs (timestamps, HTTP status codes, latency, sniffed response headers).
- If using streaming: transcript showing truncated content + last event-id or stream sequence number.
- If using structured output: full request payload and the resulting truncated/invalid response.
- Optional but helpful: SDK + version, region used, model name (if pinned).

How we will use the replay package:
- We will reconstruct request flows against traces retained in our short-term debugging logs and, if needed, replay them through the recovery cluster to validate end-to-end behavior.
- Where appropriate we will surface sanitized request/response excerpts to the customer and propose remediation or targeted reprocessing.

Customer remediation suggestions (short-run, immediate):
- If you observe 5xx/503: implement exponential backoff with jitter (example: initial 200ms, max 10s). Avoid aggressive immediate retries during the spike.
- For streaming clients: detect unexpected stream-EOF and attempt a single resume or short-range retry (resume token or sequence offset if supported). If your client cannot resume, submit the replay package and indicate 'stream-lost' with approximate offset.
- For structured outputs that appear truncated: avoid optimistic parsing on first chunk; wait for explicit end-of-response marker where possible. Consider a client-side fallback to re-request with a shorter generation length limit while we validate service completeness.

Post-incident customer-facing summary (short, clear bullets for execs):
- Root cause (customer-friendly): routing change caused a small subset of requests to hit a model variant with a regression in cache handling; this produced truncated streamed outputs and spike in 5xx.
- Scope: limited to EU routing path and small percentage of tenants; no confirmed data corruption; some requests produced incomplete responses that may require replay.
- What we fixed: rolled back the configuration change, deployed a targeted mitigation to route affected prefixes to a compatible variant, and added a temporary traffic guard to prevent the same change from reaching broader pools.
- Compensations / next steps: for customers able to validate impact via replay package, we will offer prioritized reprocessing of affected requests and a credit proposal if SLA was impacted.

Remediation and follow-ups (internal notes to coordinate with PM/Eng):
- Action items for Eng-serving-runtime: add unit/regression test for KV cache under routing variant transitions (owner: @marco; ETA: 2029-04-20).
- Action items for Platform: add a traffic guard that prevents new routing variants from receiving traffic >1% without additional canary checks (owner: @avery; ETA: 2029-04-25).
- Action items for CS: prepare targeted outreach to top 50 affected tenants with a one-click replay request form and prioritized queue (owner: Priya; ETA: 2029-04-18).

Customer email template (short):
Subject: Update: Service incident in EU region — action steps if you were affected
Hi <CustomerName>,
We wanted to let you know we investigated and resolved a service disruption that impacted a small percentage of requests in the EU region on 2029-04-12. If you observed truncated or failed responses, please reply with the replay package (tenant id, time range, example request ids) and we will prioritize verification and reprocessing.
Thanks for your patience — Priya (Redwood Customer Success)

FAQ (what to expect when you submit a replay package):
Q: How long until you validate and reprocess?
A: We will triage high-confidence customer reports within 24 hours and aim to complete reprocessing within 3 business days.
Q: Will you share logs?
A: We will share sanitized excerpts and a short verification report. Full internal logs are not shared but we will provide sufficient evidence for verification and regulatory needs where applicable.

Open questions / unresolved items (notes to self):
- Confirm whether any tenants with Dedicated capacity were affected — early signs suggest no, but need infra confirmation. (owner: Diego)
- Decide on a standard SLA credit table for incidents that require reprocessing vs those that just required customer-side retries. (owner: CS leadership)

Slack/GitHub/Jira snippets to include when escalating:
- Slack: #inc-4821 — brief timeline + link to this doc + request for eng owner.
- GH: link to proposed hotfix PR attached in linked_artifacts.
- JIRA: include INC-4821 in ticket and tag affected tenants for prioritization.

Notes on tone and length: keep the customer-facing content short and pragmatic. Avoid deep implementation detail in public-facing updates; customers who need more technical evidence should be directed to submit a replay package and ticket.

-- End of draft --

Draft checklist before publication:
- [ ] Confirm accuracy of incident window (observability team).
- [ ] Confirm final root cause language with Eng (avoid premature technical claims).
- [ ] Attach replay request form link to support reply template.
- [ ] Assign CS rep for top-affected tenants outreach.
- [ ] Post status updates in status page and #customer-updates channel.
